evidence.claim: The report says Sisi governed Egypt in an increasingly authoritarian manner, that meaningful political opposition was virtually nonexistent, and that dissent, press freedom, and assembly were tightly restricted; it also notes ANHRI suspended Egyptian operations in January 2022 after years of harassment.
evidence.title: Egypt: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: The report says Sisi governed Egypt in an increasingly authoritarian manner, that meaningful political opposition was virtually nonexistent, and that dissent, press freedom, and assembly were tightly restricted; it also notes ANHRI suspended Egyptian operations in January 2022 after years of harassment.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Annual country report with explicit 2022 summary and detailed political-rights sections.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sisi and his government rather than to a generic country baseline.
contrary_evidence: The report is retrospective and aggregates multiple episodes rather than isolating each 2022 decision.

evidence.claim: In July 2022 Sisi appointed a military general to the Supreme Constitutional Court's first deputy justice post, and the report says the 2018 election was unfair and noncompetitive, with state resources and media used to support Sisi and opposition candidates pressured to withdraw.
evidence.title: Egypt: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: In July 2022 Sisi appointed a military general to the Supreme Constitutional Court's first deputy justice post, and the report says the 2018 election was unfair and noncompetitive, with state resources and media used to support Sisi and opposition candidates pressured to withdraw.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific 2022 court-appointment detail plus election analysis in the same annual report.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Sisi's appointment power and regime entrenchment choices.
contrary_evidence: The report notes the state of emergency was suspended in 2021, but says repressive legislation remained in place.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that the planned national political dialogue was a test of whether authorities would ease a crackdown on dissent, and noted the 2013 protest law requiring prior police approval for demonstrations and tens of thousands detained for political reasons since 2013.
evidence.title: Factbox-National political dialogue in Egypt follows years of crackdowns
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that the planned national political dialogue was a test of whether authorities would ease a crackdown on dissent, and noted the 2013 protest law requiring prior police approval for demonstrations and tens of thousands detained for political reasons since 2013.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent wire reporting on a ruler-announced dialogue and the surrounding coercive legal environment.
evidence.period_fit: target-year 2022 political environment and dialogue launch
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Sisi's rule because the dialogue and protest law operated under his presidency.
contrary_evidence: The government said the crackdown targeted terrorists and saboteurs, not peaceful opponents.

evidence.claim: The report describes serious restrictions on free expression and media, internet freedom, peaceful assembly and association, and political participation, and says the government did not consistently punish officials who committed abuses.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Egypt
evidence.excerpt: The report describes serious restrictions on free expression and media, internet freedom, peaceful assembly and association, and political participation, and says the government did not consistently punish officials who committed abuses.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government country report summarizing 2022 conditions with detailed, structured findings.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level assessment under Sisi's administration, not a single personal act.
contrary_evidence: The report also says civilian authorities maintained effective control over the security forces and notes some pardon activity.

evidence.claim: Amnesty says the national human rights strategy was used as a propaganda tool to conceal repression ahead of COP27, and that authorities censored hundreds of websites, raided and closed independent media, and detained dozens of journalists while thousands remained arbitrarily detained.
evidence.title: Egypt: Human rights crisis deepens one year after national human rights strategy launched
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty says the national human rights strategy was used as a propaganda tool to conceal repression ahead of COP27, and that authorities censored hundreds of websites, raided and closed independent media, and detained dozens of journalists while thousands remained arbitrarily detained.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed rights report based on extensive documentation and direct engagement with authorities.
evidence.period_fit: target-year 2022 reform narrative and repression record
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly critiques the Sisi administration's governance and messaging.
contrary_evidence: Amnesty acknowledges a positive but very limited release of some prisoners of conscience.

evidence.claim: Amnesty reported hundreds of arrests in connection with calls for peaceful protests during COP27, with at least 151 detainees under investigation and hundreds more questioned.
evidence.title: Egypt: Arrests over calls for protests during COP27 expose reality of human rights crisis
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty reported hundreds of arrests in connection with calls for peaceful protests during COP27, with at least 151 detainees under investigation and hundreds more questioned.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights reporting with a specific detainee count and clear protest nexus.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Egyptian authorities under Sisi's control.
contrary_evidence: Authorities also released 766 prisoners over the same period, but Amnesty says arrests outpaced releases and continued to target free speech and association.

evidence.claim: HRW said Egyptian authorities detained nearly 700 people across 18 governorates between October 1 and November 14, 2022 after protest calls, and described surveillance and intimidation around COP27.
evidence.title: Egypt: Detentions, Repression Follow Protest Calls
evidence.excerpt: HRW said Egyptian authorities detained nearly 700 people across 18 governorates between October 1 and November 14, 2022 after protest calls, and described surveillance and intimidation around COP27.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent reporting with local-rights-group documentation and concrete detention counts.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sisi state and its security services.
contrary_evidence: HRW notes some detainees were released quickly, and authorities framed the crackdown as security work.

unresolved_gaps: There is no direct 2022 ruler-attributed nuclear command, safety, or crisis decision in the file.
El Dabaa evidence is mostly permits, construction milestones, and project self-reporting, not independent safety enforcement.
The package shows mediation and diplomatic statements, but not the internal decision chain or independent proof that Egypt's mediation changed outcomes.
There is little direct evidence on any offensive military option or coercive-force decision in 2022.
The chain from abuse to personal or cabinet-level accountability is thin, especially for prisons, police, and protest repression.
The limited remedial evidence is not outcome-verified; pardons and release gestures need follow-through data.
There was no live national election in 2022, so contestability and succession are inferred largely from retrospective rights reporting.
The internal effect of dialogue initiatives and jail releases on pluralism is not independently shown.
Hard verification of State Ownership Policy implementation and actual divestments by year-end is thin.
Household-level welfare effects of inflation, transfers, and bread security are incompletely tied to ruler action.
The package lacks direct ruler-level attribution for social-welfare decisions beyond ministerial and partner-mediated actions.
There is little completed-outcome evidence for 2022 on poverty, learning loss, malnutrition, and sanitation after the interventions.
Direct evidence of personal assets, beneficial ownership, procurement gains, or family enrichment is still missing.
The file has one clear public denial and several propaganda or censorship claims, but fewer independently verified false statements with explicit contradiction.
The core 2022 economic program is reconstructed from speeches, policy papers, and partial implementation steps rather than a single explicit governing program document.
Independent verification of divestment, budget execution, and durable follow-through is still thin.
